title: Sweets for some, harsh greens for others
odia:
କାହା କରମରେ ଖିରି ଖିରିସା
କାହା କରମରେ ଲଡୁ
କାହା କରମରେ ଖାରିଆ ଖଡା
ଚୋବାଇ ଚୋବାଇ ମରୁ।
literal_meaning: Some are allotted khiri and khirisa puddings, some laddus; others harsh-tasting greens—chew and chew until you die.
meaning_odia: କାହା ଭାଗରେ ସୁଆଦିଆ ମିଠା ଖାଦ୍ୟ, ଆଉ କାହା ଭାଗରେ କଷ୍ଟରେ ଚୋବାଇ ଖାଇବା ଶାଗ—ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଭିନ୍ନ ଭିନ୍ନ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି। କରମର କଥା କହି ଏହି ଅସମାନ ଭାଗ୍ୟ ଉପରେ ଖେଦ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଏ।
explanation: The repeated opening distributes very different meals to different people. Puddings and sweets stand against greens presented as an exhausting mouthful. This editorial reading hears a complaint about unequal comfort and hardship, expressed through the language of fortune.
usage_example: People compare how some have every comfort while others struggle for ordinary necessities. Someone recalls the contrast between sweets and endlessly chewed greens. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The first two lines name sweet foods; the third changes the taste and texture, and the repeated chewing slows the last line down. That movement makes unequal portions feel like unequal experiences of life.

odia_summary: କାହାକୁ ସୁଖର ଭାଗ, କାହାକୁ କଷ୍ଟର ଭାଗ—ଖାଦ୍ୟରେ ଅସମାନ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ଚିତ୍ର।
english_summary: Contrasting meals express unequal shares of comfort and hardship.
